budget.note: What the weekly household cap has to cover, category by category. Amounts are NOT stored here — they are derived at render time from public/periods.json, the generated spending history, so there is one home for every historical figure. This block carries only the classification (essential, discretionary, reserve, unknown), which dated bills and commitments belong to each category, and any owner target that should beat the historical average.
budget.classNote: ESSENTIAL is normal life with no reliable date — groceries, fuel, phones. It comes out of the weekly cap first. DISCRETIONARY is reducible. RESERVE is a real cost that does not fall inside this 90-day window and must be saved for rather than spent. DATED bills and commitments are already on the calendar as events and are subtracted from their category so nothing is paid twice.

budget.cardCaveat: The historical averages below are total household spending — chequing, cards and PayPal. The forecast deducts the weekly cap as CASH from the household chequing accounts, but only card MINIMUMS as debt service. Spending at the historical rate on the cards would therefore show a healthy cash line while the card balances grew. The cap is a cash instruction, and it only holds if the spending is actually paid for rather than carried.

interestCheck.note: The $158.55 is explained, and the question was mis-specified rather than unanswerable. Two things were wrong with the expected "about $115". It applied 26.99% to the CLOSING balance, but interest is charged on the average daily balance — on a card paid down and run back up those are different numbers. And it looked at August alone: June and July were charged below rate, at an effective 21.98% and 17.69%, leaving $45.46 uncollected; August then ran at 36.46% and collected it. Across five cycles the model implies $504.37 against $492.64 actually charged — a 2.3% gap, which is the transaction-date-versus-posting-date bias and nothing more.

counterparties.note: TD's export never names the other side of an e-transfer — outgoing reads SEND E-TFR ***GCa and nothing more. Interac's confirmation emails do name them, and sweeping both mailboxes properly took attribution from 24 of 204 to 49 — it has doubled. Every one of the 26 newly recovered transfers matches a bank row on amount and date, so this is corroboration, not guesswork.
counterparties.finding: Almost every newly recovered notification was in the bin. Gmail purges deleted mail after 30 days, so the counterparty record is being destroyed on a rolling 30-day cycle — which is the real reason coverage looked hopeless, and why it will stay poor unless something changes. It also means the previous conclusion was wrong: the notifications were not missing, they were deleted.
counterparties.action: A Gmail filter on both accounts that labels and archives mail from payments.interac.ca instead of deleting it costs nothing and makes every future transfer attributable. It cannot recover what has already been purged — everything deleted before roughly 10 July 2026 is gone.
counterparties.matching: The matcher was also wrong: it named every transfer of the same amount within four days from a single notification, and would let an incoming notification name an outgoing transfer. It now matches one notification to one transfer, nearest date first, direction enforced.

questions.q: What does the coaching activity actually net historically?
questions.detail: Q1 stays OPEN for historical P&L. Amanda's seasonal coaching takes in large e-transfers — 8 of over $3,000 totalling $42,395 in that first-pass slice; $54,213 inbound over 18 months — and she pays coaches from that inbound. Owner-stated 2026-08-29: no shop/resale/inventory business; leftover is gravy when it arrives, not Forecast income; do not invent a margin or a split of the $54,213 inbound / $19,700 unmatched outbound. Parents' dental-lab rent ended after May 2026. Unmatched outbound may be coach pay; that is not written as fact.
questions.changes: Forecast does not treat coaching e-transfers as household income. Historical net remains unknown. The income warning on this page is the planning caveat, not a derived monthly coaching-income figure. Tennis BC salary remains Forecast household income.

questions.q: Where do the coach payments leave from?
questions.detail: One coach is paid by cheque from DEBT&PAYMENTS — five cheques, $8,150, February to November 2025. But they stop in November 2025 while her sheets show $6,397.50 of coach pay between April and August 2026. Meanwhile the 30 June remittance of $9,646.25 went onto the HELOC the same day it arrived.
questions.changes: Whether pass-through money owed to coaches was spent on household debt. Also points at the account outside the captured set — the same one that may be one of the two unidentified accounts.
